channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Singapore Dollar: Downward bias holds within tight range against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann note that USD/SGD stayed firm on Monday, closing at 1.2945 after trading between 1.2906 and 1.2950, with the Singapore Dollar (SGD) Nominal Effective Exchange Rate (NEER) holding 1.68% above its mid-point.

item.title: Forex Today: US Dollar falls after soft CPI, Oil and Gold rally
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY) fell around 0.4% to 100.90 on Tuesday after softer-than-expected United States (US) inflation data weakened demand for the Greenback.

item.title: Euro gains as softer US inflation weighs on US Dollar
item.description: EUR/USD trades higher near 1.1420 on Tuesday as the US Dollar (USD) weakens following softer-than-expected United States (US) inflation data. The Euro’s recovery remains mainly driven by broad Greenback selling rather than Eurozone developments.

item.title: Chinese Yuan: Trade surplus cushions yuan against US Dollar – Commerzbank
item.description: Dr. Henry Hao at Commerzbank reports a strong upside surprise in China’s June trade data, with exports up 27% and imports 36% year-on-year, driven by global AI infrastructure demand.

item.title: USD/CHF Price Forecast: Pair pulls below 0.8100 but remains bullish
item.description: The USD/CHF tumbles by 0.70% on Tuesday, trading at 0.8093, as the latest US inflation report prompted market participants to pare hawkish bets that the Federal Reserve might cut the Fed funds rate this year.

item.title: Indonesian Rupiah: Supported by ratings yet constrained against US Dollar – OCBC
item.description: OCBC strategists Sim Moh Siong and Christopher Wong note that S&P’s affirmation of Indonesia’s BBB/A-2 ratings with a stable outlook is mildly supportive for the Indonesian Rupiah (IDR) by removing immediate downgrade risk.

item.title: Gold price jumps as US inflation knocks the US Dollar off its pedestal
item.description: Gold price surges by some 1.50% on Tuesday as US consumer inflation data came in below estimates, easing pressure on the Federal Reserve (Fed) to further tighten ahead of 2026. The XAU/USD trades at $4,050 after bouncing off daily lows of $3,983.

item.title: Singapore: Growth forecast lifted as AI tailwinds persist – UOB
item.description: UOB’s Jester Koh raises Singapore’s 2026 GDP growth forecast to 4.8% from 4.0% after strong 1H26 performance, with manufacturing and electronics leading gains on AI-related demand.

item.title: Fed’s Goolsbee: June CPI inflation data was “surprisingly benign”
item.description: Federal Reserve (Fed) Bank of Chicago President Austan Goolsbee said on Tuesday that the June Consumer Price Index (CPI) report was encouraging but cautioned against overreacting to a single month of data.

item.title: United States Dollar Index slips as soft US CPI dents Fed rate-hike bets
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY) comes under selling pressure on Tuesday after softer-than-expected United States (US) inflation data prompted traders to scale back expectations of an imminent Federal Reserve (Fed) interest rate hike.

item.title: China: Trade data upside surprise with AI demand – Deutsche Bank
item.description: Deutsche Bank strategists note that China’s latest trade figures significantly beat expectations, with both exports and imports accelerating in June. Strong global demand for AI-related and technology goods offset geopolitical pressures, widening China’s trade surplus well beyond consensus.

item.title: Japanese Yen rises as cool US CPI slashes bets on Fed rate hikes
item.description: The Japanese Yen registers gains of over 0.31% against the US Dollar as traders trim hawkish bets following a softer-than-expected US inflation report. The USD/JPY trades at 161.93 after reaching a daily high of 162.48.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: Soft US inflation lifts XAG/USD, but downside bias remains
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) trades on the front foot on Tuesday as softer-than-expected US inflation data tempers expectations of a near-term Federal Reserve (Fed) interest rate hike and pushes the US Dollar (USD) lower. At the time of writing, XAG/USD trades around $58.50, up nearly 2% on the day.

item.title: Dow Jones Industrial Average sits out the disinflation party
item.description: The June Consumer Price Index (CPI) fell 0.4% on the month against consensus for a 0.1% decline, following May's 0.5% increase, and the annual rate dropped to 3.5% from 4.2%, well under the 3.8% forecast. Core prices were flat MoM and eased to 2.6% YoY versus 2.8% expected.

item.title: US President Trump: Strait of Hormuz open to all shipping except Iran
item.description: United States (US) President Donald Trump reiterated in a Truth Social post on Tuesday, “The Strait of Hormuz is open to ALL ship traffic except for Iran.” He added that the US would impose a “FULL Blockade” only on vessels travelling to or from Iranian ports or carrying Iranian cargo.

item.title: Fed Chair Warsh reaffirms they will deliver price stability
item.description: While testifying on the Semiannual Monetary Policy Report before the US House Financial Services Committee, Federal Reserve (Fed) Chairman Kevin Warsh reiterated that the Fed is making a commitment on price stability and the goal of 2% inflation.

item.title: Australian Dollar surges amid soft US inflation
item.description: AUD/USD trades sharply higher near 0.6990 on Tuesday, approaching the psychological 0.7000 level as the US Dollar (USD) falls following weaker-than-expected United States (US) inflation figures.

item.title: Canadian Dollar climbs to four-week high on soft US CPI, rising Oil prices
item.description: The Canadian Dollar (CAD) strengthens sharply against the US Dollar (USD) on Tuesday, drawing support from softer-than-expected US inflation data and rising Oil prices amid escalating tensions in the Middle East.

item.title: Natural gas: European prices climb on Gulf risks – ING
item.description: ING’s Warren Patterson and Ewa Manthey report that European natural gas benchmarks are rising as Middle East developments threaten LNG flows from the Persian Gulf.

item.title: Gold rises 2% as soft US CPI cools Fed rate-hike bets
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) rebounds sharply on Tuesday, erasing losses recorded on the previous day after softer-than-expected US inflation data eased expectations of a near-term Federal Reserve (Fed) interest rate hike.

item.title: China: AI exports boom and muted FX impact – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale economists describe China’s June trade surplus of $125.62bn, driven by 27% yoy export growth and 36% import growth, with AI-related high-tech shipments up over 50%.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar soars to one-month high as US CPI undershoots
item.description: NZD/USD jumps to a one-month high on Tuesday as traders digest the latest US inflation data, which came in softer than expected and reduced expectations of an imminent Federal Reserve (Fed) interest rate hike. At the time of writing, the pair trades around 0.5820, up nearly 1.23% on the day.

item.title: Why Japan's massive foreign assets could be the Japanese Yen's long-awaited catalyst
item.description: The Japanese Yen (JPY) continues to trade in defensive territory, with the USD/JPY pair pinned near a historic 40-year high around 162.00. However, in a striking divergence from rising global yields, Japanese Government Bonds (JGBs) have begun outperforming.

item.title: Oil: Short positions vulnerable to squeeze – TD Securities
item.description: Bart Melek at TD Securities argues that money managers are heavily short crude based on what he views as misread market conditions, including pessimism on China demand and expectations of an oil glut.

item.title: Canada: Cyclical rebound and steady BoC stance – RBC
item.description: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC) economist Claire Fan expects Canada’s economy to rebound in Q2 2026, supported by resilient household spending, recovering business investment and expanding net trade.

item.title: British Pound strengthens after US CPI surprises to the downside
item.description: The British Pound (GBP) strengthens against the US Dollar (USD) on Tuesday after US inflation data surprised to the downside, reducing expectations of a near-term Federal Reserve (Fed) interest rate hike.

item.title: Indonesian Rupiah : Under pressure with hawkish BI bias – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale notes Bank Indonesia’s (BI) reaction function is driven by the Indonesian Rupiah (IDR) and exchange rate stability. The report says the Rupiah faces pressure from a stronger US Dollar (USD) and hawkish Federal Reserve (Fed) pricing, with stress around USD/IDR 18,000.

item.title: Hungary: Growth outlook getting brighter – ING
item.description: ING economists Peter Virovacz and Frantisek Taborsky turn more optimistic on Hungary’s growth outlook, noting positive surprises in high-frequency data and stronger consumption. They still project 1.5% GDP growth in 2026 but now see clear upside risks.

item.title: Euro jumps as softer-than-expected US CPI cools bets on rate hikes
item.description: EUR/USD snaps a two-day losing streak on Tuesday as softer-than-expected United States (US) inflation data weighs on the US Dollar (USD) and prompts traders to scale back expectations of a near-term Federal Reserve (Fed) interest rate hike.

item.title: European Union: Growth potential re-rated – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities’ Julie Ioffe and James Rossiter argue that the European Union already possesses key ingredients for stronger long-term growth, including wealthy consumers, productive workers, deep private savings and solid fiscal capacity.
